source.snippet: Ask HN: 'Has Codex gotten slower recently?' — 6 points, posted 2026-06-23. No body text beyond the title, but 6 upvotes in early hours suggests resonance among developers actively using Codex (a paid OpenAI product).

problem_statement: Developers paying for AI coding assistants (specifically OpenAI Codex) are experiencing perceived performance degradation and lack visibility into whether slowdowns are systemic, their own configuration, or temporary — causing lost productivity and uncertainty about tool reliability.
target_segment: Software developers and engineering teams at companies paying for AI coding assistant subscriptions (Codex, Copilot, Cursor, etc.).
notes: Buyer signal: users of Codex are on paid plans. The pain is reliability/observability — they cannot tell if slowness is their problem or the provider's. Adjacent opportunity: a status/performance monitoring dashboard for AI coding tools (similar to Downdetector but for LLM API latency and quality). Signal strength capped at 2 — single data point, no body text, could be transient.
